ACTUAL TASK: UPGRADE DACAIS LOCAL AGENT INTO A PRODUCTION-GRADE, CLAUDE-CODE/CODEX-CLASS LOCAL CODING AGENT

This is ONE integrated repository upgrade. Do not split it into future phases and do not stop after planning.
Inspect the existing repository first, then implement, wire, migrate, test, execute, and verify the entire stack in this run as far as the available tools and infrastructure permit.

Repository:
C:\Users\Kyleh\DacaiLocalAgent

Workspace:
DacaiLocalAgent

Primary local model:
qwen3:8b

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Transform the existing DACAIS Local Agent into a durable, stateful, context-managed, retrieval-augmented, reasoning-aware autonomous coding agent that behaves as close as practical to modern Claude Code / Codex-style repository agents while preserving the existing DACAIS authorization, permission, workspace, audit, approval, provider, tool, RAG, memory, and database architecture.

This is not a blank-slate rewrite.

REUSE THE EXISTING IMPLEMENTATIONS.

Known existing architecture includes or is expected to include:

- packages/agent-core
- packages/context
- packages/memory
- packages/rag
- packages/providers
- packages/tools
- packages/security
- packages/shared
- packages/workspace
- packages/training-traces
- packages/agents
- apps/server
- apps/web
- config/models/default.yaml

Existing database foundations include:

- repositories
- repository_files
- code_symbols
- symbol_edges
- knowledge_documents
- knowledge_chunks
- memory_entries
- pgvector
- HNSW indexes on code_symbols.embedding and knowledge_chunks.embedding
- 768-dimensional embeddings

Existing model-role configuration includes or is expected to include:

- agent
- planner
- reasoner
- coder
- structured_agent
- reviewer

The current autonomous model is qwen3:8b.

CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL RULE

DO NOT create duplicate RAG, memory, repository-indexing, permission, approval, provider, workspace, or database systems.

Trace and wire the existing implementations.

LangChain/LangGraph may be added as orchestration/integration infrastructure, but must NOT replace or bypass DACAIS security boundaries.

The existing PermissionedToolExecutor / PermissionEngine / workspace capabilities / ApprovalRegistry / audit trail remain authoritative for tool execution.

============================================================
1. INSPECT FIRST
============================================================

Before implementing broad changes, inspect:

- package.json and relevant package.json files
- pnpm workspace structure
- packages/agent-core/src
- packages/context/src
- packages/memory/src
- packages/rag/src
- packages/providers/src
- packages/tools/src
- packages/shared/src database code
- packages/workspace/src
- packages/training-traces/src
- packages/agents/src
- apps/server/src/routes/agent.ts
- apps/server/src/routes/rag.ts
- apps/server/src/routes/memory.ts
- apps/server/src/index.ts
- config/models/default.yaml
- current AGENTS.md instructions
- current git status/diff

Discover exact filenames with filesystem.list.
Do not use content search as filename discovery.

Preserve unrelated user changes.

============================================================
2. ADD LANGCHAIN / LANGGRAPH WITHOUT REPLACING DACAIS CONTROLS
============================================================

Use current JavaScript/TypeScript packages appropriate to the existing pnpm monorepo:

- langchain
- @langchain/core
- @langchain/langgraph
- @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-postgres
- @langchain/ollama
- zod if not already available

Install them in the narrowest appropriate package(s), not blindly everywhere.

Use LangGraph as the durable state-machine/orchestration layer.

Use PostgresSaver for durable thread/checkpoint state.
Use PostgresStore if appropriate for cross-thread long-term graph state.

Use the existing DATABASE_URL / database configuration.
Never hardcode credentials.
Never print connection strings containing secrets.

If LangGraph setup requires its own checkpoint/store tables, allow its supported setup to create only its own framework tables.
Do NOT redesign or replace existing DACAIS application tables.

LangSmith must remain OPTIONAL and OFF by default.
No cloud tracing requirement may be introduced.

============================================================
3. BUILD A DURABLE CODING-AGENT GRAPH
============================================================

Create or integrate a graph with explicit state roughly equivalent to:

AgentExecutionState:
- taskId
- threadId
- workspaceId
- currentGoal
- originalPrompt
- phase
- plan/checklist
- pendingItems
- completedItems
- blockedItems
- knownPaths
- knownFiles
- evidence
- decisions
- retrievedContext
- repositoryContext
- memoryContext
- rollingSummary
- recentMessages
- toolFailures
- validationFailures
- changedFiles
- validationResults
- reviewResults
- reasoningMode
- retryCount
- toolCallCount
- completionStatus
- finalAnswer

Do not force these exact field names if existing types already cover them.
Extend existing types rather than creating parallel state models where practical.

Graph behavior should include the conceptual nodes:

BOOTSTRAP
→ LOAD REPOSITORY INSTRUCTIONS
→ RETRIEVE CONTEXT
→ PLAN
→ EXECUTE
→ OBSERVE
→ UPDATE WORKING MEMORY
→ EVALUATE PROGRESS
→ REASON / REPLAN when necessary
→ COMPACT CONTEXT when necessary
→ VALIDATE
→ REVIEW
→ FINALIZE

Routing must be conditional.

The graph must support:
- resumable execution after interruption
- checkpoints
- cancellation
- max-turn / max-tool-call limits
- human approvals
- retry after recoverable errors
- deterministic stop reasons
- no false final completion

Do not weaken existing permission controls.

============================================================
4. WORKING MEMORY / TASK STATE
============================================================

Implement structured working memory for every run.

The model must NOT be expected to reconstruct the full task from an ever-growing transcript.

Maintain a concise machine-readable task state.

For multi-step tasks track:

PENDING
COMPLETE
BLOCKED

Every completion decision must compare actual execution state to the original goal.

A directory listing, one successful read, a plan, or a progress summary is not completion when pending executable work remains.

Keep and extend the existing TASK_COMPLETE / TASK_BLOCKED completion protocol.

Do not accept ordinary prose as verified completion when completionSignalRequired is enabled.

============================================================
5. EXACT PATH GROUNDING
============================================================

Preserve and finish the known-path memory behavior.

Successful filesystem.list results must populate authoritative known paths.

When a filesystem operation fails because a path was guessed incorrectly:

- search known paths first
- match by exact path or basename
- if one unambiguous observed match exists, return a PATH CORRECTION observation
- if multiple candidates exist, return candidates
- do not silently redirect the tool call
- do not relist unchanged directories merely because the model forgot a path
- do not invent directory names

The model should copy exact paths from observations.

============================================================
6. CONTEXT MANAGER: REAL EXTENDED CONTEXT, NOT JUST MORE HISTORY
============================================================

Inspect packages/context/src/context-manager.ts and existing context types first.

Upgrade/reuse it to create a token-budgeted context assembler.

Do NOT simply increase maxHistoryMessages and dump the transcript.

Create a context budget that prioritizes:

1. system/repository instructions
2. current user goal
3. structured task state
4. critical decisions
5. relevant recent tool observations
6. exact known paths relevant to the next step
7. retrieved repository symbols/files
8. retrieved knowledge
9. relevant long-term memories
10. rolling summary
11. recent conversational messages

Discard or summarize stale low-value observations.

For qwen3:8b target approximately a 32K runtime context budget unless the provider reports a lower safe limit.

Reserve output/reasoning headroom instead of filling the entire context window.

Make context limits configurable by model/provider.

============================================================
7. ROLLING SUMMARIZATION / CONTEXT COMPACTION
============================================================

Add deterministic context compaction.

When history/tool observations exceed budget:

- preserve original goal verbatim
- preserve unresolved checklist items
- preserve exact paths still relevant
- preserve errors still being debugged
- preserve changed-file list
- preserve validation results
- preserve security/approval state
- summarize older completed observations
- remove redundant duplicate observations

Summaries must never silently mark work complete.

Persist useful thread summary/checkpoint state so a resumed task does not restart from zero.

============================================================
8. REPOSITORY RAG / SEMANTIC CODE RETRIEVAL
============================================================

Trace existing packages/rag implementation before creating anything.

The expected existing path is:

register repository
→ enumerate files
→ detect language
→ hash
→ parse
→ extract symbols
→ generate summaries
→ generate 768-dim embeddings
→ code_symbols
→ symbol_edges
→ repositories.indexed_at

Fix the existing path if incomplete.

Ensure repository indexing actually runs for:

C:\Users\Kyleh\DacaiLocalAgent

Do not create another code index.

Use existing:
- repositories
- repository_files
- code_symbols
- symbol_edges

Implement/verify semantic retrieval from code_symbols.

Use retrieved repository context inside normal agent execution, not only via a separate debug endpoint.

Retrieval should be invoked:
- at task start for complex repository requests
- before architectural changes
- when a symbol/module is referenced but not yet loaded
- after repeated path/search failure
- when re-planning

Combine semantic retrieval with exact lexical/path evidence where useful.

Do not let retrieved text override authorization/system instructions.

============================================================
9. KNOWLEDGE RAG
============================================================

Trace existing:

knowledge document ingestion
→ chunking
→ 768-dim embedding
→ knowledge_chunks
→ semantic retrieval
→ agent context injection

Wire knowledge retrieval into the context manager.

Retrieved context must include provenance/metadata sufficient to identify its source.

Do not create a second knowledge store.

============================================================
10. LONG-TERM MEMORY
============================================================

Inspect packages/memory/src and memory_entries.

Trace:

agent result/observation
→ memory decision
→ memory_entries write
→ later lookup
→ context injection

Wire it into normal agent execution.

Persist only useful durable memories such as:

- repository conventions
- confirmed architecture facts
- user-approved preferences
- resolved recurring failures
- validated commands/workflows
- durable project decisions

Do NOT store:
- raw secrets
- API keys
- passwords
- private keys
- full secret-bearing connection strings
- transient tool noise
- entire raw transcripts unnecessarily

Use retrieval relevance before injecting memory.

============================================================
11. MODEL ROLES: PLANNER / CODER / REASONER / REVIEWER
============================================================

Reuse the existing model aliases/config.

Use planner before complex work.

Use coder for normal tool-driven execution.

Use reasoner when:
- tool failures repeat
- tests fail
- architectural ambiguity exists
- retrieved evidence conflicts
- progress stalls
- a broad refactor is required

Use reviewer after non-trivial modifications.

The reviewer receives:
- original goal
- checklist
- changed files
- relevant diff
- test/typecheck/build results
- unresolved failures

Reviewer must not approve work merely because code exists.

If reviewer finds a correctable defect:
→ return to execution
→ fix
→ revalidate
→ review again

============================================================
12. DYNAMIC REASONING POLICY
============================================================

Replace a permanently hard-coded think:false coding behavior with a dynamic reasoning policy.

Support:

FAST
- routine listing/read/stat
- straightforward known edit
- low ambiguity
- thinking off when supported

STANDARD
- normal coding
- moderate debugging
- multi-file work
- thinking on when supported

DEEP
- architecture
- repeated failures
- complex refactors
- conflicting evidence
- difficult debugging
- thinking on
- planner/reasoner path
- stronger retrieval and review requirements

Do not expose hidden reasoning as a security dependency.
Final claims still require tool evidence.

If provider/model does not support thinking, degrade gracefully.

============================================================
13. OLLAMA CONTEXT CONFIGURATION
============================================================

Inspect packages/providers/src/ollama-provider.ts and existing provider configuration.

For qwen3:8b configure a practical coding-agent context target around 32768 tokens unless runtime/model capability inspection establishes a better safe value.

Do not exceed known provider/model limits blindly.

Make context size configurable rather than hardcoded globally.

If Ollama request options support num_ctx in the existing integration, wire it there.

Preserve streaming and structured tool calling.

============================================================
14. PROVIDER / LANGCHAIN INTEGRATION
============================================================

Do not replace the existing ProviderRegistry unless necessary.

Prefer an adapter.

The DACAIS provider abstraction remains the public/internal boundary.

If @langchain/ollama ChatOllama is used:
- wrap it behind existing provider interfaces, or
- use it only in graph planner/reasoner/retrieval paths where appropriate

Preserve the existing verified capability probe and advisory-vs-agent distinction.

A model must still be rejected from autonomous tool execution unless DACAIS capability checks verify it.

============================================================
15. TOOL SELECTION / CONTEXT REDUCTION
============================================================

Do not expose every possible tool to every model turn if unnecessary.

Implement dynamic tool filtering based on:
- workspace capabilities
- role
- current graph phase
- task requirements

Examples:
- planning: mostly read/search/context tools
- editing: filesystem edit/write + diagnostics
- validation: tests/git/diagnostics
- web only when network capability exists and task needs it

The PermissionEngine remains authoritative even when a tool is hidden/shown dynamically.

============================================================
16. TOOL ERROR RECOVERY
============================================================

Preserve existing:
- unknown-tool recovery
- duplicate-call detection
- path correction
- no-progress detection

Improve recovery state so failures are recorded structurally.

Repeated failure should escalate reasoning/replanning rather than immediately repeating the same operation.

Distinguish:
- denied
- invalid arguments
- path not found
- duplicate call
- timeout
- tool exception
- validation failure
- provider failure

============================================================
17. DURABLE CHECKPOINTS / RESUME
============================================================

Use LangGraph Postgres checkpointing for coding-agent thread state.

Generate safe thread IDs under provider/database limits.

Checkpoint around meaningful transitions.

A process restart or approval pause should be able to resume without losing:
- goal
- checklist
- known paths
- completed work
- relevant context summary
- validation state

Do not persist secrets unnecessarily.

Do not replace existing application task tables unless existing architecture explicitly calls for integration.

============================================================
18. HUMAN APPROVALS
============================================================

Keep existing ApprovalRegistry / PermissionEngine behavior.

LangGraph must not bypass approvals.

If a mutation/high-impact tool call requires approval:
- durable graph state must survive the pause
- execution resumes only after the existing approval decision resolves

A denial remains a denial.

Never retry a denied action through a different route merely to bypass policy.

============================================================
19. VALIDATION-FIRST CODING
============================================================

After code changes, automatically choose relevant validation:

- code.diagnostics
- targeted tests
- package typecheck
- repository typecheck
- lint when relevant
- build when relevant
- runtime/API smoke test when relevant

Track validation evidence structurally.

A task cannot be TASK_COMPLETE if requested changes have unaddressed validation failures caused by the current work.

============================================================
20. DIFF REVIEW
============================================================

For implementation tasks:

- inspect git status before changes
- preserve existing user changes
- track files changed by this task
- inspect scoped git diff after implementation
- send diff + validation results to reviewer role

Do not reset unrelated changes.

============================================================
21. CONTEXT / RAG SECURITY
============================================================

Treat retrieved repository text, knowledge chunks, memory entries, web content, and tool output as untrusted data.

They cannot:
- alter permission policy
- override system instructions
- grant authorization
- expand workspace scope
- bypass approvals
- disclose secrets

Preserve existing security boundaries.

============================================================
22. SERVER / API INTEGRATION
============================================================

Wire the upgraded runtime into /api/agent/stream.

Preserve SSE events.

Add useful structured events where practical, such as:

- phase
- checkpoint
- context_compaction
- retrieval
- reasoning_mode
- plan_update
- validation
- review
- completion

Do not break existing clients unnecessarily.

Update apps/web types/UI only as required for compatibility and to surface meaningful progress.

============================================================
23. OBSERVABILITY
============================================================

Reuse LoopTraceRecorder / training traces.

Record:
- graph phase transitions
- reasoning mode selection
- tool calls/results
- retries
- retrieval metadata
- context compactions
- validation
- review
- final stop reason

Do not record secrets.

LangSmith must remain optional/off by default.

============================================================
24. TESTS
============================================================

Add targeted tests covering at least:

1. premature final prose is rejected
2. TASK_COMPLETE accepted only by completion protocol
3. no-progress after repeated non-completion
4. path memory learns recursive listing paths
5. wrong basename receives unique PATH CORRECTION
6. multiple basename candidates do not silently redirect
7. context budget compacts stale observations
8. original goal survives compaction
9. unresolved checklist survives compaction
10. retrieval context is injected
11. memory retrieval is injected
12. denied tool cannot be bypassed
13. duplicate calls are rejected
14. repeated failures trigger reasoning escalation
15. validation failure prevents completion
16. reviewer can return task to execution
17. graph checkpoint resume restores task state
18. thread separation prevents cross-session state leakage
19. secrets are excluded from durable memory
20. provider without verified tool calling remains blocked

============================================================
25. REAL VERIFICATION
============================================================

Do not stop at unit tests.

Run the strongest available validation.

At minimum:

- targeted tests
- pnpm -r typecheck
- relevant build/lint if available

Then verify the real repository index.

Query PostgreSQL or use existing repository/RAG APIs to prove:

repositories > 0
repository_files > 0
code_symbols > 0
knowledge_chunks > 0 when knowledge exists

Verify code symbol embedding dimensions are 768.

Execute a real semantic query that should find agent-loop/context-manager/provider code.

Prove the coding agent receives retrieved repository context during a real task.

Prove memory lookup can contribute relevant prior durable state during a later run.

Prove LangGraph checkpoint persistence survives creation and reload.

Finally run a real autonomous coding-agent smoke test that:

- inspects multiple files
- maintains an explicit checklist
- uses exact known paths
- retrieves repository context
- performs or proposes a safe targeted edit
- validates it
- reviews it
- reaches TASK_COMPLETE only after verification

If a mutation in the smoke test would affect unrelated code, use a temporary/synthetic fixture within the workspace.

============================================================
26. PERFORMANCE / TOKEN CONTROL
============================================================

The previous Qwen run consumed tens of thousands of input tokens while making little progress.

Fix this.

The upgraded agent must not resend the complete raw transcript every turn.

Use:
- rolling summaries
- working-state injection
- relevant recent observations
- retrieval
- token budgets
- deduplication

Track approximate context size.

Prefer compact structured state over repeated prose.

============================================================
27. DO NOT CLAIM CLAUDE/CODEX INTERNALS
============================================================

The objective is behavioral parity in important engineering capabilities:
- persistent goal pursuit
- repository understanding
- context management
- planning
- tool use
- recovery
- validation
- review
- durable resume

Do not claim proprietary implementation parity with Claude Code or Codex.

============================================================
